Dispute: Manner of Mohamed Oufkir's death, 16 August 1972
Moroccan position: Official state account: suicide, following the collapse of the coup he had orchestrated.
Other position: Family account (his daughter Malika Oufkir): multiple gunshot wounds — reported variously as three to the back and one to the neck, or wounds across several organs — inconsistent with self-infliction, implying execution by loyalist officers.
Current assessment: Unresolved. No autopsy or forensic record has been consulted by this project. Distinguish the disagreement in fact (how many wounds, where) from the disagreement in interpretation (suicide vs execution).
Why the sources disagree: The party that controlled the death scene and the official record — the Moroccan state — is also the party whose legitimacy the alternative account (execution by the regime) would undermine. This is not a French/Spanish/Moroccan colonial-era dispute; the usual three-tradition template doesn't apply cleanly to a post-1961 state-vs-family dispute, which is itself worth noting.

Dispute: Zaian dead at El Herri, 13 November 1914
Moroccan position: 182 (the 1991 HCAR/state monument repeats the French figure)
Current assessment: A French floor, not an independently corroborated total. The monument is not independent corroboration.
Why the sources disagree: Not a French-vs-Moroccan dispute in the usual sense — both traditions currently repeat the same uncorroborated number.

Dispute: Who decided the 1953 deposition of Mohammed V
French position: El Glaoui and the notables took the initiative
Moroccan position: Paris and the Résidence orchestrated it; El Glaoui's role was instrumental, not originating
Current assessment: Settleable from Résidence–Paris correspondence, May–August 1953, not yet consulted.
Why the sources disagree: Each tradition places responsibility with the actor least sympathetic to it.

Moroccan position: Reported higher; no Moroccan primary count located yet by this workspace
Other position: German 2,000–3,000 (embarrassing France served Berlin's interests during the 1905–1911 crisis period)
Current assessment: Unresolvable on present evidence. State the range and the definitions; do not collapse to one figure.
Why the sources disagree: No party to the bombardment had an incentive to count accurately: France to minimise a scandal, Germany to maximise one.

French position: Killed in a clash with French-allied partisans
Moroccan position: Killed by his own son Hassan (most repeated); alternatively, in a clash with a party his sons had joined
Current assessment: Disputed. Three different claims routinely collapsed into one. Treat the patricide narrative with particular caution.
Why the sources disagree: The patricide version is narratively convenient in a way that should itself prompt scrutiny, not confidence.

Spanish position: 7,875 / 8,180 / 8,668 / 13,363 — competing totals depending on whether Moroccan Regulares are counted
Current assessment: Definitional, not merely evidentiary. State the range and the definitions.
Why the sources disagree: The count depends on who is counted as Spanish — Spanish sources are, uniquely, unreliable on their own casualties.

French position: Oufkir named by a French court
Other position: Dlimi, Mossad and CIA involvement alleged but not established
Current assessment: Documents exist and are withheld. A different category from unknown.
Why the sources disagree: This is not primarily a source-conflict; it is an access-conflict. Distinguish withheld from unknown, per standing rule 5.
